glyfp

The glyfp package represents glycans as fingerprints for comparison and modeling. It provides binary and count fingerprints of connected glycan substructures and optional pretrained SweetNet, GlycanGT and GIFFLAR embeddings through fp_motif_binary(), fp_motif_count(), fp_sweetnet(), fp_glycangt() and fp_gifflar(). Each function exposes only options relevant to its method. Inputs can be glyrepr structures or text in formats supported by glyparse.

Installation

glyfp is under local development and is not yet available from CRAN, R-universe, or a remote repository. Install it from this package directory:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::repo_add(glycoverse = "https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev")
pak::local_install(".")

Note: Tips and troubleshooting for the meta-package glycoverse also apply here: Installation of glycoverse.

Role in glycoverse

glyfp is being developed as part of the Glycoverse ecosystem. It builds on glyrepr for glycan structures, glyparse for text parsing, and glymotif for substructure extraction and counting. Its fingerprints are intended as inputs to glycan comparison, clustering, and predictive workflows.

Example 

library(glyfp)

Encode complete glycans using the built-in glydb motif dictionary:

glycans <- c("Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-")
fp <- fp_motif_count(glycans)
lengths(fp)
#> [1] 3173 3173
fp[[1]][c("Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-")]
#>          Gal(b1- Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- 
#>                3                2

The repeated disaccharide is counted twice, including overlapping occurrences. Use fp_motif_binary(glycans) for presence/absence. The default motif_dict = "fixed" keeps coordinates aligned across separate calls. Set motif_dict = "dynamic" in either motif function to build a dictionary from the current batch, including motifs outside glydb. Dynamic dictionaries may differ between batches; combine inputs in one call for aligned coordinates. Inputs must specify complete structures, including the reducing-end anomer. Use fp_circular_binary() or fp_circular_count() for hashed residue neighborhoods or fp_residue_pair() for endpoint environments and graph distances, with fixed dimensions across batches. The getting-started vignette explains all methods, pretrained checkpoints and supported chemistry.
